name: moa_normalize_config
notes: MoA config normalizer (real port src/hermes_cli/moa_config.c::moa_normalize_config linked; LIVE twin hermes_cli/moa_config.py::normalize_moa_config). V event = canonical summary (default/active/sorted presets with enabled, refs provider/model list, aggregator provider/model, max_tokens). Covers: legacy flat preset, named presets, name strip-and-keep, unknown default_preset -> first-preset fallback, active_preset clearing, disabled preset w/ explicit temps+tokens, multi-slot refs, empty-name preset dropped -> legacy path. KNOWN DIVERGENCES (inputs avoided, NOT hidden): (1) REAL PORT BUG/FAP — the port's hardcoded defaults (moa_default_reference_models/moa_default_aggregator: nvidia_nim/z-ai/glm-5.2 + 9 nim slots) do NOT match LIVE _default_reference_models/DEFAULT_MOA_AGGREGATOR (openrouter/anthropic/claude-opus-4.8). Repro: input '{}' -> C canonical agg=nvidia_nim/z-ai/glm-5.2 vs PY agg=openrouter/anthropic/claude-opus-4.8 (also hits every incomplete-slot degradation, e.g. {"reference_models":["m1"]}). All gated inputs therefore carry fully-specified slots so no default-models fallback fires. (2) Temps: C coerces null/default temperatures to numbers (0.6/0.4); LIVE keeps None — temperatures excluded from the canonical value except where explicitly numeric. Non-object payloads ('{}', '[]', 'not json') also fall into the diverging defaults path and are ungated for the same reason. (3) REAL PORT BUG/FAP — off-by-one trailing-strip in moa_normalize_config/moa-clean paths: `pe = s + strlen(s); while (pe > s && isspace(pe[-1])) *--pe` was written as a check of *pe (the NUL), so TRAILING whitespace is never removed from preset names / default_preset / active_preset, while LIVE uses str.strip(). Repro input {"presets":{"  spaced  ":{...}},"default_preset":"spaced","active_preset":"spaced"} -> C keeps key 'spaced  ', default='spaced  ', active='' (C=7cbf9fc8ae4d8552) vs LIVE default/active/key all 'spaced' (PY=25a1d5082513). Fix: test pe[-1] before decrement (i.e. start at end-of-string minus one).
